behavior_anomalies.why: The logged patient count exceeds the hospital’s 40 beds, but no overflow, diversion, transfer, discharge, or other capacity constraint appears. The count then continues rising to 336, implying unlimited accumulation of hospital patients.

The run begins receiving patients while ventilation allocation is at zero, but it never records zero allocations, refusals, waiting patients, deaths, transfers, or any other consequence for patients dependent on ventilation. The same omission persists as the patient count grows to 336, far beyond the hospital's stated 40-bed capacity.

The run repeatedly attempts delivery despite zero starting supply, but the log never records ventilator availability, ventilator allocation limits, denied ventilation, or an order/escalation. The patient population continues progressing without any observable effect from the exhausted resource.

The logged hospital has 40 beds, but the patient count rises to 41 with no overflow, diversion, transfer, or capacity-limit consequence. The count then continues growing to 336, implying that the hospital accommodates far more patients than its physical capacity.
The actor records four patients despite starting at zero and having no stated enabling cause. The same unsupported progression continues throughout the log, reaching 382 patients by t74.

action admit-flu-patients-v1 refuses up front with check 'the hospital has enough available beds' on actor.components.hospital_capacity.available_beds, a stock the actor's own activity consumes. Fix with three changes: (1) the action only STARTS the activity (sets a status such as 'driving'), with no check on that stock and no progress or consumption effects; (2) add a process that, every tick while the status is active and the stock is above zero, makes one tick of progress and consumes the stock; (3) add a process that switches the status to a stopped/failed value when the stock is at or below zero, so the actor discovers it by observation.
